identification.summary: XinXin (also tracked as Black Technology and changqixinyun) is described by PRODAFT as a Chinese-speaking cybercriminal group that has operated the Lucid phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform since mid-2023, selling subscriptions via Telegram, and that has also used the Lighthouse and Darcula phishing kits [S1][S2]. Lucid delivers smishing through Apple iMessage and Android RCS to bypass SMS filters, and was reported to have hit 169 entities in 88 countries [S1].
identification.firstObserved: 2023-06 (Lucid operated by XinXin since mid-2023, per PRODAFT as relayed by The Hacker News) [S1]
identification.notes: Reporting is secondary coverage of the PRODAFT Lucid report; the primary document could not be opened. Lucid, Lighthouse and Darcula are described as an interconnected Chinese-language smishing ecosystem; vendors track developers separately (LARVA-246 for Darcula, LARVA-241 for Lighthouse) [S2]. Do not merge XinXin with other Lighthouse-related actors without further evidence.

attribution.confidence: Not state-linked in the cited sources; PRODAFT characterizes XinXin as a Chinese-speaking financially motivated group (vendor assessment) [S1].
attribution.basis: PRODAFT assessment relayed by The Hacker News: Lucid operated by XinXin, with developer tracked as LARVA-242, a key XinXin figure [S1]. Netcraft observed overlaps between Lucid, Lighthouse and Darcula infrastructure and tooling [S2].

objectives: Financial gain: theft of credit card data and personally identifiable information via smishing, and monetization through subscription sales of PhaaS access [S1].

sectors: Consumers / general public (brand impersonation of postal, toll and government services)
targeting.notes: Lucid reportedly hit 169 entities in 88 countries, mainly Europe, UK and US [S1]. Netcraft (Sept 2025) found Lucid-hosted phishing URLs targeting 164 brands in 63 countries and Lighthouse URLs targeting 204 brands in 50 countries, over 17,500 domains combined [S2].

capabilities.summary: Lucid is sold by subscription through a Telegram channel (about 2,000 members) with weekly licensing, and delivers smishing via iMessage and RCS to evade SMS filtering [S1]. Phishing pages gate access by mobile user agent, proxy country or configured path, serving a generic fake storefront to non-targets [S2]. XinXin also uses Darcula v3 and Lighthouse, and monitors and supports similar PhaaS services [S1].

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking cybercriminal group XinXin; developer tracked as LARVA-242 [S1].
diamond.capability: Lucid PhaaS, Darcula v3 and Lighthouse kits; iMessage/RCS smishing; victim gating [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram sales channel; large numbers of phishing domains (over 17,500 across Lighthouse and Lucid) [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Consumers and brands across 60-90 countries, mainly Europe, UK, US [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Financially motivated criminal ecosystem operating from China-linked, Chinese-speaking communities; no state tasking evidenced in cited sources [S1].
diamond.technology: Mobile messaging (iMessage, RCS, SMS), phishing kits, Telegram, payment card systems [S1][S2].

Relationship between XinXin and Smishing Triad / Lighthouse operators unverified.
Individual identities, hierarchy and monetization details unconfirmed beyond the vendor summary.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Operational environment: mobile messaging channels (iMessage, RCS, SMS) are the delivery vector and consumers are the victims [S1]. Threat evaluation: financially motivated PhaaS operator selling to affiliates, not state-tasked per cited sources [S1]. MLCOA: continued smishing impersonating postal, toll and government brands to harvest cards and PII, potentially reaching DoD personnel and families as consumers [S1]. MDCOA: reuse of the kit infrastructure against government-themed lures aimed at personnel, which the cited sources do not show. Candidate indicators: Telegram sales activity, newly registered impersonation domains, victim-gated landing pages [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: treat as a criminal threat to personnel via personal devices rather than to mission networks; track vendor and Netcraft domain reporting [S2]. Authorities: response is largely law-enforcement and civil rather than military cyberspace operations. Mission assurance: emphasize personnel awareness and reporting of smishing on personal and work phones. Coordination: share indicators with DC3, service CSSPs and commercial providers.

provenance.importedSummary: XinXin is a Chinese-speaking threat actor known for its phishing-as-a-service platform, Lucid, which targets global organizations to steal credit card details and personally identifiable information through smishing campaigns. The group employs advanced techniques such as exploiting Rich Communication Services and Apple's iMessage protocol to bypass traditional SMS filters. XinXin also develops and utilizes other phishing kits like Lighthouse and Darcula, facilitating large-scale phishing operations with automated tools and evasion techniques. The group operates a structured hierarchy and monetizes stolen data while actively supporting the development of similar PhaaS services.
